key_insight: A physics-informed neural network couples turbine-blade geometry and flow-field optimisation to match prescribed surface-pressure targets.
engineering_relevance: The method translates experimental-origin blade-loading data into geometric modifications for aerodynamic design.
method: Constrain the inverse problem with the 2D steady compressible Euler equations.
Use pressure-target continuation and alternate geometry updates with flow re-adaptation.
Optimise blade-surface positions and orientations through a differentiable representation.
evidence_signal: On the LS89 cascade with 28 experimental-derived pressure targets, pressure-side and suction-side RMS fitting errors reached 1.13% and 2.21% of inlet total pressure; independent SharC verification reproduced the principal pressure trends.
watch_item: The 2D inviscid formulation does not resolve viscous or turbulent effects, and verification retained discrepancies near the trailing edge.
paper_title: A physics-informed neural network method for pressure-driven turbine-blade optimization
